sources.entry: Go: _Code a database in 45 steps: a series of test-driven small coding puzzles_

summary.title: Code a database in 45 steps (Go)
summary.one_liner: You learn database internals by building a database from scratch in Go, one small test-driven puzzle at a time.
takeaways: The project is 45 test-driven puzzles, most under 50 lines of code, building a database with no dependencies.
Topics covered include KV storage engines, LSM-Tree indexes, SQL, concurrent transactions and ACID.
An accompanying paid book gives detailed explanations and background (the author says it helps fund the project).
The page lists table-of-contents entries for index (08) and concurrency (09) among the steps.
This is the first Trial of Code project from 2025, with more planned.
summary.summary: The page describes Trial of Code, a series of 45 small test-driven coding puzzles that guide readers through building a database from scratch in Go with no dependencies. The puzzles are mostly under 50 lines each and cover key areas such as KV storage engines, LSM-Tree indexes, SQL, concurrent transactions and ACID. An optional book with detailed explanations and background is available for sale. The page lists a partial table of contents, including Index (08) and Concurrency (09).
